name: Moving averages (20 and 50 day)
short: How far the price sits above or below its average price of the last 20 and 50 days.

explainer.measures: The average closing price over the last 20 and 50 trading days, and how far today's price is from each. It smooths out daily noise to show the general level prices have been trading at.
explainer.calc: Add the last N closing prices and divide by N. The app shows the gap between today's price and that average, as a percentage.
explainer.settings: 20 days for the short-term level, 50 days for the medium-term level. 200 days is common for the long term.
explainer.limits: Averages lag: they only describe the past and turn after prices have already moved. In sideways markets the price crosses its average often without any lasting change.

name: RSI (Relative Strength Index)
short: How strong recent gains have been compared with recent losses, on a 0 to 100 scale.

explainer.measures: The balance of up days against down days over the last 14 trading days. Readings near 100 mean gains dominated; near 0, losses dominated. 70 and 30 are the levels most often quoted.
explainer.calc: Average gain and average loss over 14 days are smoothed with Wilder's method; RSI = 100 − 100 ÷ (1 + average gain ÷ average loss).
explainer.settings: 14 days is standard. Shorter periods react faster and swing to extremes more often.
explainer.limits: In a strong trend RSI can stay above 70 or below 30 for weeks. A reading describes recent momentum, not what comes next.

name: MACD
short: The gap between a fast and a slow average, and whether that gap is widening or narrowing.

explainer.measures: The difference between the 12-day and 26-day exponential averages (the MACD line), compared with its own 9-day average (the signal line). The histogram is the gap between the two.
explainer.calc: MACD = EMA(12) − EMA(26). Signal = EMA(9) of MACD. Histogram = MACD − Signal.
explainer.settings: 12, 26 and 9 days are the standard settings.
explainer.limits: Built from averages, so it lags. The histogram changes sign often in choppy markets.

name: Bollinger Bands (%B)
short: Where the price sits inside a band two standard deviations either side of its 20-day average.

explainer.measures: A band around the 20-day average whose width grows and shrinks with volatility. %B places today's price in the band: 0 is the lower band, 1 the upper band, 0.5 the middle.
explainer.calc: Middle = 20-day average. Upper and lower = middle ± 2 standard deviations of the last 20 closes. %B = (price − lower) ÷ (upper − lower).
explainer.settings: 20 days and 2 standard deviations are standard.
explainer.limits: Prices can ride along a band for long stretches. The band describes recent variability only.

name: 50-day high and low
short: How far the price is from its highest point of the last 50 trading days.

explainer.measures: The highest and lowest prices of the last 50 trading days, and the distance of today's price from the high.
explainer.calc: Highest high and lowest low over the last 50 daily bars.
explainer.settings: 50 days here; 52 weeks (about 250 days) is the other common window.
explainer.limits: A new high or low says where price has been, not where it will be.

name: Volume vs average
short: Today's trading volume compared with the average of the previous 20 days.

explainer.measures: How busy trading was today compared with normal. 2x means twice the usual number of shares or coins changed hands.
explainer.calc: Today's volume ÷ average volume of the previous 20 days.
explainer.limits: Not available for indices. Crypto volume from one exchange is only a slice of the whole market.

name: ATR (Average True Range)
short: The typical size of a day's price move over the last 14 days, as a % of price.

explainer.measures: How much the price usually moves in a day, including overnight gaps.
explainer.calc: True range = the largest of high − low, |high − previous close| and |low − previous close|, smoothed over 14 days with Wilder's method.
explainer.limits: It measures the size of moves, not their direction.

name: Stochastic oscillator
short: Where today's close sits within the high–low range of the last 14 days, 0 to 100.

explainer.measures: Whether the price is closing near the top or bottom of its recent range.
explainer.calc: %K = 100 × (close − 14-day low) ÷ (14-day high − 14-day low).
explainer.settings: 14 days; a 3-day average of %K is often drawn as %D.
explainer.limits: Swings between extremes quickly in volatile markets.

name: Williams %R
short: The stochastic idea on a −100 to 0 scale: how close the close is to the recent high.

explainer.measures: How close today's close is to the highest high of the last 14 days.
explainer.calc: %R = −100 × (14-day high − close) ÷ (14-day high − 14-day low).
explainer.limits: Same as the stochastic oscillator: it moves fast and stays at extremes in trends.

name: CCI (Commodity Channel Index)
short: How far the typical price is from its 20-day average, scaled by its usual deviation.

explainer.measures: Distance of price from its average in units of typical deviation; most readings fall between −100 and +100.
explainer.calc: CCI = (typical price − 20-day average of typical price) ÷ (0.015 × mean deviation). Typical price = (high + low + close) ÷ 3.
explainer.limits: Unbounded, so extreme readings vary by instrument.

name: ADX (Average Directional Index)
short: How strong the current trend is, whatever its direction, on a 0 to 100 scale.

explainer.measures: Trend strength. Low readings mean prices are moving sideways; higher readings mean a more persistent trend, up or down.
explainer.calc: Compares upward and downward moves over 14 days (+DI and −DI) and smooths their difference with Wilder's method.
explainer.limits: Says nothing about direction and reacts slowly.

name: Rate of change
short: The % change in price over the last 12 trading days.

explainer.measures: Plain momentum: how much the price has changed over a fixed window.
explainer.calc: ROC = (close − close 12 days ago) ÷ close 12 days ago × 100.
explainer.settings: 12 days here; 9, 14 and 25 are also common.
explainer.limits: Very sensitive to the single price it compares against.

name: Exponential moving average (20 day)
short: A 20-day average that gives more weight to recent prices.

explainer.measures: The recent price level, reacting faster than a simple average.
explainer.calc: EMA today = price × k + EMA yesterday × (1 − k), with k = 2 ÷ (N + 1).
explainer.limits: Still lags, and its faster reaction means more false turns.

name: On-Balance Volume
short: Adds volume on up days and subtracts it on down days.

explainer.measures: Whether trading volume has leaned towards up days or down days.
explainer.calc: A running total: add the day's volume when the close is higher than yesterday's, subtract it when lower. Here we show its change over 20 days as a share of all volume traded in that time.
explainer.settings: No settings; usually read over a few weeks.
explainer.limits: A single huge-volume day can dominate it, and it ignores how far the price moved.

name: VWAP
short: Needs minute-by-minute prices, so it has no daily reading here.
note: Needs minute-by-minute prices, so it has no daily reading here.

name: Ichimoku Cloud
short: Price compared with the Ichimoku cloud.

explainer.measures: Whether price is above, inside or below the cloud built from past highs and lows.
explainer.calc: Span A = midpoint of the 9- and 26-day high–low midpoints; Span B = the 52-day midpoint. Both are drawn 26 days ahead, so today's cloud comes from 26 days ago.
explainer.limits: Built for daily markets with gaps; on round-the-clock coins the spans are just periods of days.

name: Parabolic SAR
short: Trailing dots that follow the trend.

explainer.measures: Whether price is above or below a trailing level that speeds up as a move continues.
explainer.calc: Each day the SAR moves towards the extreme price by an acceleration factor starting at 0.02, rising by 0.02 to 0.2. It flips side when price crosses it.
explainer.limits: Flips often when prices move sideways.

name: Stochastic RSI
short: Where RSI sits within its own recent range, 0 to 100.

explainer.measures: How today's RSI compares with its highest and lowest values over 14 days.
explainer.calc: (RSI − lowest RSI in 14 days) / (highest − lowest) × 100.
explainer.limits: Very jumpy: it often swings from 0 to 100 within days.

name: Money Flow Index
short: A volume-weighted version of RSI, 0 to 100.

explainer.measures: The balance of buying and selling pressure, using both price and volume.
explainer.calc: Typical price (high + low + close) / 3 times volume gives money flow. MFI = 100 − 100 / (1 + up-day flow / down-day flow) over 14 days.
explainer.settings: 14 days; 80 and 20 are the levels people commonly mark.
explainer.limits: Readings can stay above 80 or below 20 for a long time in a strong move.

name: Chaikin Money Flow
short: Average of volume-weighted close position over 20 days.

explainer.measures: Over 20 days, whether closes sat near the highs or lows of their days, weighted by volume.
explainer.calc: Sum of (close-location multiplier × volume) over 20 days, divided by total volume. Ranges from −1 to +1.
explainer.limits: Like A/D, it ignores gaps between one day's close and the next day's open.

name: Awesome Oscillator
short: Gap between the 5-day and 34-day averages of each day's midpoint.

explainer.measures: Whether recent prices are above or below the longer-run average.
explainer.calc: 5-day simple average of (high + low) / 2 minus the 34-day one. Shown here as a percentage of price so coins can be compared.
explainer.limits: Lags the price, as all moving-average measures do.

name: Momentum
short: Price change over the last 10 days.

explainer.measures: How far the price has moved over a fixed number of days.
explainer.calc: (Today's close − close 10 days ago) / close 10 days ago, shown as a percentage.
explainer.settings: 10 days is common; some use 12 or 14.
explainer.limits: It depends only on two prices, so the start date matters a lot.

name: Double EMA
short: A faster-reacting 20-day average.

explainer.measures: How far price sits from an average that reacts faster than a normal EMA.
explainer.calc: DEMA = 2 × EMA(20) − EMA of that EMA(20). Shown as the price's % distance from it.
explainer.limits: Faster means more false turns in choppy markets.

name: Triple EMA
short: An even faster 20-day average.

explainer.measures: How far price sits from a triple-exponential average.
explainer.calc: TEMA = 3 × EMA − 3 × EMA(EMA) + EMA(EMA(EMA)), over 20 days. Shown as % distance.
explainer.limits: Very responsive, so it overshoots in choppy markets.

name: Keltner Channels
short: Bands at ±2 ATR around a 20-day average.

explainer.measures: Where price sits between bands set by the average daily range.
explainer.calc: Middle = EMA(20); bands = middle ± 2 × ATR(10). Position is 0% at the lower band, 100% at the upper.
explainer.limits: Price can ride along a band for a long time.

name: Pivot points
short: Shown on the chart: tap the S/R button on a card and choose Pivot points.
note: Shown on the chart: tap the S/R button on a card and choose Pivot points.

name: Donchian Channels
short: Where the close sits in the 20-day high–low channel.

explainer.measures: How close the price is to its 20-day high or low.
explainer.calc: (Close − 20-day low) / (20-day high − 20-day low) × 100.
explainer.limits: A single spike sets the channel edge for 20 days.

name: Supertrend
short: A line set a multiple of ATR away from price.

explainer.measures: Whether price is above or below a volatility-based trailing line.
explainer.calc: Bands at the day's midpoint ± 3 × ATR(10). The line follows the lower band while price stays above it and switches to the upper band when price closes below.
explainer.limits: In sideways markets it switches sides frequently.

name: Aroon
short: How recent the 25-day high is versus the 25-day low.

explainer.measures: Whether new highs or new lows have been more recent.
explainer.calc: Aroon Up = 100 × (25 − days since 25-day high) / 25; Aroon Down likewise for the low. The oscillator is Up − Down, from −100 to +100.
explainer.limits: It only looks at timing, not at how big the moves were.

name: TRIX
short: Daily change of a triple-smoothed average.

explainer.measures: The direction of a heavily smoothed trend, with day-to-day noise filtered out.
explainer.calc: Take a 15-day exponential average three times in a row, then its 1-day % change.
explainer.limits: The heavy smoothing makes it slow to respond to turns.

name: Ultimate Oscillator
short: Close position blended across 7, 14 and 28 days, 0 to 100.

explainer.measures: Where closes sit within their true ranges, across three time spans at once.
explainer.calc: Buying pressure (close − true low) / true range, averaged over 7, 14 and 28 days and weighted 4:2:1.
explainer.limits: Blending periods smooths it, so short sharp moves show less.

name: Fibonacci retracement
short: A drawing tool rather than a reading, so it has no daily number here.
note: A drawing tool rather than a reading, so it has no daily number here.

name: Historical volatility
short: How much prices swung over 20 days, as a yearly figure.

explainer.measures: The size of daily price swings, scaled to a year so it can be compared across coins.
explainer.calc: Standard deviation of daily log returns over 20 days × √365 × 100 (coins trade every day).
explainer.limits: It describes the past; volatility can change quickly.

name: Accumulation/Distribution
short: Volume weighted by where each day closed in its range.

explainer.measures: Whether volume has come with closes near the day's high or near its low.
explainer.calc: Each day, a multiplier from −1 (closed at the low) to +1 (at the high) times volume, added to a running total. We show its 20-day change as a share of volume.
explainer.limits: Ignores gaps between days, so a big overnight move can be missed.

name: Elder-Ray Index
short: Highs and lows compared with a 13-day average.

explainer.measures: How far buyers pushed the high above, and sellers pushed the low below, the 13-day average.
explainer.calc: Bull power = high − EMA(13); bear power = low − EMA(13). Shown as % of price.
explainer.limits: One unusual day can swing both readings.

name: Know Sure Thing (KST)
short: Weighted sum of four smoothed rates of change.

explainer.measures: Price change across short and long spans in one number.
explainer.calc: Rates of change over 10, 15, 20 and 30 days, each smoothed (10, 10, 10, 15 days) and weighted 1, 2, 3, 4, then added.
explainer.limits: The number itself has no fixed scale; its sign and turns are what people read.

name: Vortex Indicator
short: Upward versus downward movement over 14 days.

explainer.measures: Whether today's highs stretch further from yesterday's lows than lows from yesterday's highs.
explainer.calc: VI+ = sum |high − previous low| / sum true range; VI− = sum |low − previous high| / sum true range, over 14 days. We show VI+ − VI−.
explainer.limits: Choppy markets make the two lines cross often.

name: Chande Momentum Oscillator
short: Up-day gains minus down-day losses, from −100 to +100.

explainer.measures: The balance between gains on up days and losses on down days.
explainer.calc: (Sum of gains − sum of losses) / (sum of gains + sum of losses) × 100 over 14 days.
explainer.limits: Like RSI, it can stay at extremes during long trends.

name: Hull Moving Average
short: Alan Hull's low-lag 20-day average.

explainer.measures: How far price sits from a smooth average designed to lag less.
explainer.calc: Weighted average over √20 days of (2 × WMA(10) − WMA(20)). Shown as % distance.
explainer.limits: Can overshoot after sharp moves.

name: ZigZag
short: A drawing tool rather than a reading, so it has no daily number here.
note: A drawing tool rather than a reading, so it has no daily number here.

name: P/E ratio
short: Needs company earnings; coins don't have them.
note: Needs company earnings; coins don't have them.

name: Beta
short: Needs a market index to compare with; not available for coins yet.
note: Needs a market index to compare with; not available for coins yet.
